Senator Tan Parker highlights education access and career pathways in recent posts
Senator Tan Parker posted several messages between October 12-14 focusing on educational opportunities and workforce development in Texas.
Senator Tan Parker, who represents Texas's 12th Senate district, used his social media platform this week to highlight the importance of exploration, education, and career opportunities in Texas. Parker, a Republican elected to the State Senate in 2023 after succeeding Angela Paxton, shared messages emphasizing both historical reflection and practical steps for expanding access to higher education and workforce training.
On October 12, Parker posted about Columbus Day: "Today, on Columbus Day, we reflect on the courage to explore, the spirit of discovery, and the determination to pursue new horizons. That same pioneering spirit helped build Texas and America, a belief in opportunity, the promise of freedom, and the power of faith and https://t.co/ch01V7eYxc".
Two days later, he highlighted a visit to a Dallas-area educational institution: "Great visit to @DISDCI Dr. Edwin Flores Career Institute North! Incredible to see students gaining real-world skills in high-demand fields like healthcare, technology, manufacturing, and skilled trades. Expanding career pathways and connecting education to opportunity remain key https://t.co/MzaIwAjPy8" (October 14).
Later that same day on October 14, Parker encouraged participation in Free College Application Week for Texas residents: "A stronger Texas starts with opportunity! It’s Free College Application Week! Now through October 18, Texas residents can apply to public colleges and universities with NO application fees through ApplyTexas! Education opens doors, empowers the next generation, and builds a https://t.co/gMQibKAHPv".
Parker's remarks reflect ongoing legislative attention in Texas toward broadening access to higher education and technical training programs as ways to support workforce development across the state.
